Guidance & outlook: With GDP growth projected at 6.6% in FY27, a formidable domestic consumption base, and one of the most ambitious public-infrastructure investment cycles in our history, the structural tailwinds for Beaconʼs business lines have rarely been stronger.

As Awarded by PRIME Database for deals achieved in FY 2025 Asset Under Administration (AUA) accumulated on a cumulative basis across all services offered. executed, registering arise of 10.69% y-o-y basis.

The attrition rate increases to 20% in FY26 is acknowledged and is a board-level priority for FY27, being addressed through enhanced career pathways, competitive compensation, and expanded wellness programmes.
Growth & demand: Indiaʼs bond market is forecast to roughly double to ₹120 lakh crore by FY30, the AIF ecosystem is accelerating, GIFT City is growing rapidly, and security trusteeship demand is rising structurally.

Security trustees, acting as collateral and enforcement agents on behalf of lender consortia, have seen expanding demand driven by the growth of private credit, infrastructure finance, and structured lending.

Opportunities SEBIʼs push for active trustee monitoring, the large-corporate borrowing framework, the reduced ₹10,000 minimum investment ticket, and the projected growth of Indiaʼs corporate-bond market beyond ₹120 lakh crore by FY 2030 together represent a multi- year structural demand driver for the core debenture-trusteeship business.
Margins & costs: The Company delivered an EBITDA margin of 40.27%, a level that reflects the genuine operating leverage of our asset-light model, and a profit after tax of ₹817.55 Lakhs at a PAT margin of 25.68%.

Threats Predatory pricing by new entrants can raise client-acquisition costs and pressure fee realisations in the short term, even though the long-term viability of undercapitalised trustees is questionable.

EBITDA stood at ₹1,281.78 Lakhs at a margin of 40.27%, reflecting the operating leverage inherent in the model as revenue scales on a predominantly fixed and semi-fixed cost base, with employee benefit expenses at a modest 21.61% of revenue.
Capex & expansion: The shares of 66.67% in UTAI have been acquired by Beacon Trusteeship Limited in the capacity of a member and not as a holding company.

Weaknesses The Indian debt market, at ₹226 lakh crore in outstanding size, is very large relative to Beaconʼs current mandate base, and continued investment in business development, technology, and talent is required to capture a larger share of new issuances and fund setups.
Revenue from operations reached ₹3,183.19 Lakhs, driven by the expansion of the AIF trusteeship mandate base, strong deal flow in debenture trusteeship, and accelerating securitisation activity.
Balance sheet & cash: Basic earnings per share were ₹4.53, achieved on a completely debt-free balance sheet with a net worth of ₹5,325.27 Lakhs.

SEBIʼs framework requiring large corporates to raise a minimum share of incremental borrowing through the bond market, together with the reduction of the minimum investment ticket to ₹10,000, is broadening both the supply of, and investor base for, corporate bonds, and each issuance requires a SEBI- registered debenture trustee.

The balance sheet as at 31st March 2026 carries a net worth of ₹5,325.27 Lakhs funded entirely through internal accruals, nil long-term borrowings, and total assets of ₹6,297.64 Lakhs including strategic investments in group subsidiaries, with IPO proceeds being deployed across technology infrastructure, service-offering expansion, working capital, and strat…
Risks & challenges: A material economic slowdown that reduced bond issuance, AIF fundraising, or NBFC lending could moderate the growth of the mandate pipeline, though the diversified product mix mitigates this risk.

Mitigation of Risk / Risk Management The Board of Directors assesses and classifies risks across operational, financial, regulatory, technology, and human-capital domains on a continuous basis, under the oversight of the Audit Committee and with inputs from the Internal Auditor, Statutory Auditor, and Company Secretary.
Human Resources Employee Benefit Expenses declined to 21.61% of revenue (FY25: 29.05%) demonstrating operating leverage as revenue scaled while employee costs were managed efficiently.
